claim: Path-scoped triggers, statistical delta gates (Welch's t + effect size), and concurrency.cancel-in-progress are the core patterns for reliable CI eval gates
quote: Gates fail only when both conditions hold: Mean score dropped below baseline, Welch's t-test yields p < 0.05, Effect size exceeds noise floor (~0.03 on normalized scales)

claim: Model providers push silent base-model updates and production traffic distributions shift — pre-deploy snapshot gates miss both; the fix is a two-layer architecture (pre-release gate + continuous production monitoring)
quote: Model providers update base models silently. Retrieval pipelines drift as knowledge bases grow. Traffic distributions shift as real users find edge cases your test suite never imagined.

claim: assert_test() raises an assertion error in pytest CI builds when a metric falls below its threshold; evaluate() collects results without failing and should not be used in CI
quote: assert_test() is built for CI/CD and raises an assertion error when a metric falls below its threshold, while evaluate() is for scripts and notebooks and collects results without failing.

claim: Judge calibration requires Pearson r > 0.7 vs human labels before scaling; threshold calibration must be based on real historical data rather than arbitrary metrics
quote: Target a Pearson correlation above 0.7 between the judge's scores and domain expert verdicts; below that threshold, you are measuring something but don't know if it correlates with whether users experience the product as working.

claim: Production monitoring uses 5-10% traffic sampling; 50 expertly curated examples outperform 500 auto-generated ones; each production failure should become a test case within 48 hours
quote: fifty expertly curated examples with clear acceptance criteria will tell you more than 500 auto-generated examples

claim: promptfoo-action supports path-scoped triggers, fail-on-threshold, repeat/repeat-min-pass for flaky-eval tolerance, and native PR comments with pass/fail counts
quote: fail-on-threshold: Suite pass percentage requirement (0-100); repeat / repeat-min-pass: Handle non-deterministic LLM outputs

claim: CI eval dataset should include production logs (tagged by difficulty), domain-expert annotations, known regressions converted to test cases within 48h, and adversarial inputs
quote: Define test suites with representative cases for each scenario, sourced from production logs and labeled with expected behaviors

claim: Four evaluation approaches in the pyramid: benchmark testing, code/rule-based checks, LLM-as-judge, and human-in-the-loop; each has distinct cost and trust tradeoffs
quote: Approach: Benchmark Testing (initial model screening), Code-Based/Rule-Based (deterministic requirements), LLM-as-a-Judge (nuanced text quality), Human-in-the-Loop (high-risk domains)

claim: Langfuse experiment-action@v1 supports dataset_version pinning and blocks PRs when experiment score misses the threshold defined in the experiment script, compared against a versioned baseline
quote: When an experiment score misses your threshold, the workflow fails so reviewers can see the regression before merging.

claim: Start judge calibration with 25–50 human-labeled outcome cases (not expected scores), target < 5% combined false positive/negative rate before scaling
quote: Human-labeled dataset (25-50 test cases marked for real outcomes, not metric scores); Metric alignment targeting <5% combined false positive/negative rates

claim: Start with a capable LLM judge (GPT-4o class), validate alignment against human annotations before scaling; define success criteria numerically (e.g., ROUGE-L ≥ 0.40, 70%+ positively rated)
quote: start with capable models like gpt-5.5 and validate alignment with human labels before optimizing for cost. Once the LLM judge reaches a point where it's faster, cheaper, and consistently agrees with human annotations, scale up.

claim: Braintrust offers dedicated GitHub Action with PR comments and quality gates; Promptfoo requires one YAML file and integrates in ~15 minutes; Phoenix and Langfuse require custom Python scripts for CI orchestration
quote: Braintrust's CI/CD quality gates are a standout feature — define minimum score thresholds for your evals, and Braintrust blocks deployments that fail, preventing regressions from being shipped.

claim: Arize Phoenix experiments API gate uses experiment.get_evaluations()['score'].mean() > 0.8 as the CI threshold, triggered via GitHub Actions on every push
